One person was killed in an attack against an Iranian cargo ship in the Strait of Hormuz, Tehran claimed, though it notably didn’t identify the perpetrator.

Iranian state media outlet IRNA quoted the governor of Qeshm as blaming the attack on a “terrorist enemy,” though he didn’t specify which. The hesitancy is notable, as most previous attacks are quickly blamed on the United States.

Actual Article Body:

Amazon will temporarily halt its use of 21 Air, the operator of the Prime Air cargo jet that overshot a runway and plowed into a van at Miami International Airport last week, killing five people, after numerous safety complaints about the company came to light.

The online retail giant confirmed the pause to NBC News, saying its decision is a result of the probe into the fatal Sept. 6 plane crash as well as a review of “some of the surrounding circumstances.”

“After the tragic incident last weekend, we’ve spent time supporting the investigation and reviewing some of the surrounding circumstances, and we’ve decided to pause our operations with 21 Air, the operator of Flight 7598,” Amazon spokesperson Kelly Nantel told the outlet.
